secret.description: Elijah Bledsoe hands a parcel of stolen goods to a man at the Kitchen at 9:30 PM.

people.name: Ellsworth Bidwell
people.relationshipToVictim: a childhood friend of the victim from the same block

secret.description: Ellsworth Bidwell goes through the papers in the Victim's Suite from 7:00 PM to 7:30 PM while the victim is downstairs.
Domenica Marchetti is not the person the register says. Nothing is hidden about the evening; the lie is in the paperwork.
Gustav Wehrle drinks alone in the Bar from 9:30 PM to 10:00 PM and will claim to have been anywhere else.
Margaret Sweeney slips out to the Street from 9:30 PM to settle with a bookmaker.
Filomena Lanza is alone with Margarethe Dettweiler in the Service Stairs from 9:00 PM to 9:30 PM, and kills Margarethe Dettweiler at 9:30 PM.

motive.description: blamed the victim for a ruin

method.name: strangling with a cord
method.bodyEvidence: A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.

Margarethe Dettweiler was found on the Service Stairs. The coroner puts death between 9:00 PM and 9:30 PM. A ligature furrow across the throat. Three fibres of hemp in the skin.
A length of sash cord is missing from the Kitchen. A cut end of the same hemp is still tied to the fitting it was taken from.
The passenger elevator was out of order from 7:00 PM to 8:00 PM. Anyone changing floors in that time used the service stairs.
The service stairs were whitewashed that afternoon. There is whitewash on Ellsworth Bidwell's sleeve; Ellsworth Bidwell was on the stairs at 8:00 PM.
The service stairs were whitewashed that afternoon. There is whitewash on Domenica Marchetti's sleeve; Domenica Marchetti was on the stairs at 7:00 PM.
Domenica Marchetti's papers do not hold up. A letter addressed to a name nobody at the hotel has heard used.
Found in the Victim's Suite: A promissory note for $4,000 signed by Domenica Marchetti, endorsed to Margarethe Dettweiler, three months past due.
Edward Brennan says Margarethe Dettweiler told Domenica Marchetti that Friday was the end of it, one way or the other.
Found in the Front Desk: A clipping about the failure of Filomena Lanza's business, with Margarethe Dettweiler's name underlined twice in pencil.
Edward Brennan says Filomena Lanza said Margarethe Dettweiler had taken everything and would be made to feel it.
